summary: Identical follow-up turn experiences p99 latency and 504s after initial prompt — KV/prefix cache warmup degeneration
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports large P99 latency increase and intermittent 504s on second conversational turns that are text-identical to the first turn. Behavior started after a canary deploy on 2026-03-09 and is reproducible for a subset of sessions in Acme Analytics' dedicated pool. Impact: Increased user-visible latency and occasional stream disconnects for conversational flows that reuse exact prompt prefixes. This affects Acme's core conversational product and is blocking an in-flight demo.

Impact: ~20% of identical follow-up turns show >2s p50 -> p99 skew, with a p99 rising from 620ms to ~3.8s for affected requests. 504s observed at ~0.6% of identical-turn requests in the last 72h window.

Priority & next steps: Sev1 customer-impacting. SRE assigned to investigate cache warmup and prefix lookup path; engineering will prepare a patch after reproducer validated in staging.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer sends conversational turn A (prompt length ~60 tokens) to model redwood-open-13B in prod us-east-1.
2) Immediately send an identical follow-up turn A' (same exact tokens, new request id).
3) Observe response times and stream behavior for the second request.
4) Repeat with ~200 parallel sessions to reproduce sampling of failures.

Note: Acme provided request IDs and sample payloads in attached logs.
observed_behavior: Second (identical) turn shows elevated p95/p99 latency and occasional 504s. Metrics from customer telemetry: p50 640ms -> p50 850ms, p95 1.2s -> 2.7s, p99 0.62s -> 3.8s for identical-followups; 504s spike to 0.6% (baseline 0.02%). Server logs show kvcache miss->fallback + repeated prefix backfills in the serving node's logs immediately before 504s.
expected_behavior: Identical follow-up turns should hit KV/prefix cache hot path and return at near-identical latency to the initial prompt (modulo tokenization differences). No increase in 5xx rate is expected for warm cache scenarios.

investigation_notes:
Timeline: Issue surfaced 2026-03-09 after a canary that changed the kvcache lease refresh behavior (decreased aggressive background refresh).

Findings so far:
- Spike in kvcache miss_rate on shard 12 concurrent with p99 spikes.
- Backfills for identical prefixes showed duplicated inflight backfill requests across multiple threads on the same node, leading to serialized KV reads and occasional timeouts.
- The new canary reduced the TTL refresh frequency for prefetched prefixes; combined with a new suffix-key hashing change introduced a stale mapping window where a warm prefix could be evicted and then immediately re-requested by identical follow-ups.
- Heap snapshots on node-7 show transient memory pressure around the same time, triggering an eviction job that removed recently-warmed prefixes.

Hypothesis: A race between reduced TTL refresh, shard-level eviction, and duplicated backfill in-flight requests causes identical follow-up turns to miss the cache and then block on serialized backfill logic. Serialization amplifies latency and increases chance of backfill timeout (manifesting as 504).

Experiments run:
- Reproduced locally by lowering kvcache.refresh_interval and inducing artificial memory pressure; observed identical p99 pattern.
- Increased kvcache.prefetch_dedupe window in staging; p99 dropped ~40% in synthetic test.

Next investigative tasks:
- Capture per-request backfill concurrency counts for all affected nodes.
- Add detailed tracing for lease refresh events and eviction triggers.
- Validate patch that reintroduces a small refresh buffer and dedupes concurrent backfills.
workaround:
For Acme (dedicated pool) applied temporary mitigations on 2026-03-11: 1) Increased kvcache.refresh_interval back to pre-canary value for Acme's pool. 2) Enabled backfill_dedupe=true (experimental flag) to collapse concurrent backfills. 3) Recommended customer to route high-variance sessions to a pinned model-variant to avoid cross-variant evictions.
These reduced error rate to ~0.05% and lowered observed p99 by ~35% for a 24h window.
resolution:
Patch proposal: 1) Revert the aggressive decrease of kvcache TTL refresh in canary and add a controlled refresh jitter to prevent synchronized eviction. 2) Add server-side dedupe for in-flight prefix backfills with a small concurrency cap per-shard. 3) Add a soft-cache-protect window after warmup to prevent eviction for N seconds.
Deployment plan: apply change to staging (done 2026-03-13), run canary on 5% of prod (scheduled 2026-03-15), then 25% rollout if no regressions, full rollout 2026-03-17.
Follow-ups: update runbook, add automated synthetic tests that exercise identical-turn warm-cache scenarios, and create telemetry alert for concurrent backfill counts exceeding threshold.
Status: Patch is in review (PR linked) and staging validation passed for synthetic traffic.
